description: Polish Matura math syllabus (podstawa programowa) mapped to long-form (8+ minute) chaptered videos in the AI Math Long-Form style. One video per syllabus chapter, in textbook order.

legend.bonus: poza programem (enrichment, outside the strict syllabus)

video_skeleton: intro — the central question + the raw pattern
roadmap — list the chapters that follow
master build — the whole idea once, slow, uninterrupted
worked examples — the SAME template, 5-9 times, numbers only change
pattern check — read the pattern back off the results
big case — one deliberately large / awkward example
the reason — why the key step can never fail
recap — restate every example + the one-line reason

video.title: Every exponent rule from one idea
video.angle: aᵐ·aⁿ, (aᵐ)ⁿ, a⁻ⁿ, a^(1/n) are all forced once you decide exponents must keep adding when you multiply.
covers: an exponent as a repeated-multiplication count
aᵐ·aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ worked for several m, n
why a^(1/n) must be the n-th root
the single 'add the exponents' law underneath all of it

video.title: Logarithms are just exponents, read backwards
video.angle: log turns multiplication into addition because exponents already do; every log law is an exponent law in disguise.
covers: log b x defined as 'the exponent'
log(ab) = log a + log b worked on numbers
why a slide rule / decibels / Richter work
the one exponent law behind every line

video.title: The triangle inequality, everywhere
video.angle: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| is just 'a detour is never shorter', seen on the number line and in the plane.
covers: |a+b| vs |a|+|b| on the number line for several sign patterns
the same statement as vectors / a triangle
recap: no detour beats the direct step

video.title: Why compound interest runs away from simple interest
video.angle: adding a percentage of a growing amount beats adding a percentage of a fixed amount — and the gap itself grows.

video.title: Why the digit-sum tricks work (3, 9, 11)
video.angle: 10 leaves remainder 1 mod 9 and remainder −1 mod 11, so a number and a signed digit-sum share a remainder.
covers: digit-sum test for 3 and 9 on several numbers
why 2 and 5 only need the last digit
the place-value reason behind all of them

video.title: The short-multiplication formulas are pictures
video.angle: (a+b)², (a−b)², a²−b² are areas of a cut-up square; the algebra just records the pieces.
covers: (a+b)² as a square cut four ways
(a−b)² as a square with a corner removed
a²−b² as an L-shape rearranged into a rectangle
recap: every identity is a rearrangement

video.title: Polynomial arithmetic is base-x arithmetic
video.angle: adding, multiplying and long-dividing polynomials is column arithmetic with no carrying, in base x.
covers: a number written in base 10 vs a polynomial in x
long division of numbers next to long division of polynomials

video.title: Why fractions need a common denominator
video.angle: you can only add things that are the same size; a common denominator makes the pieces the same size.
covers: why bd always works (and lcm is just tidier)
the same idea for rational expressions

video.title: Why a negative multiplier flips an inequality
video.angle: multiplying by −1 reflects the number line; order reverses under a reflection.
covers: a < b shown on the number line
multiply both sides by 2, by 1/2 — order kept

video.title: Where the quadratic formula actually comes from
video.angle: completing the square turns every quadratic into (x + p)² = q; doing it with letters IS the formula.
covers: the discriminant as 'what's under the root'

video.title: Why |x| = a always splits into two cases
video.angle: two points sit at distance a from 0; an absolute-value equation is a distance statement.

video.title: Why P(a) = 0 means (x − a) divides P(x)
video.angle: divide P(x) by (x − a); the remainder is a constant, and that constant is P(a).
covers: a case where the remainder isn't 0
recap: roots and factors are the same information

video.title: Why solving a rational equation can invent fake answers
video.angle: multiplying through by a variable expression can multiply by zero, which is not a reversible move.
covers: a simple rational equation solved cleanly
one where x = 2 makes a denominator 0
checking every candidate back in the original
recap: always test against the original

video.title: Why an inverse is a reflection across y = x
video.angle: the inverse swaps input and output; swapping coordinates reflects the graph across y = x.
covers: a function as an input→output machine
swapping the columns of a table
y = x² needing a restricted domain

video.title: Why f(x − a) shifts a graph right, not left
video.angle: to get the same output, x must be larger by a — so every point moves right by a.
covers: f(x) vs f(x−2) point by point
a f(x) and f(bx) as stretches
the 'what x makes this input' reason
recap chart of all six moves

video.title: Why a line's slope is the same everywhere on it
video.angle: similar triangles under any two points on a line have equal rise-over-run.
covers: a different pair of points, same ratio
y = mx + b read off a graph
perpendicular slopes multiplying to −1 (a rotated triangle)

video.title: Why every parabola is symmetric about x = −b/2a
video.angle: completing the square rewrites y as a(x − h)² + k; squaring is symmetric about h.
covers: the axis at x = −3 confirmed by a table

video.title: Why a degree-n polynomial has at most n roots
video.angle: each root peels off a factor (x − a) and drops the degree by one; you can only do that n times.
covers: factoring a cubic step by step
why you run out after n peels
complex roots of a real polynomial coming in conjugate pairs
a degree-4 example with 2 real + 2 complex

video.title: Why a graph hugs an asymptote but never touches it
video.angle: the gap to the asymptote is a fraction whose denominator blows up; a nonzero-over-huge is never zero.
covers: the gap written as an explicit expression
a slant asymptote by polynomial division
a case where the curve DOES cross (and why that's allowed away from ∞)

video.title: Why exponentials outrun every polynomial
video.angle: each step multiplies by a fixed factor; multiplicative growth eventually beats any fixed power.
covers: 2ˣ vs x², x³, x⁵ in a table
the ratio 2ˣ / xⁿ over successive steps
e as the base where the rate equals the value

video.title: Gauss's trick, and why it always works
video.angle: pair the ends: first + last = second + second-last = ... ; n/2 pairs of the same total.
covers: the pairing picture for odd n

video.title: Why 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ... = 1
video.angle: each term is half the remaining gap to 1; the leftover halves every step and vanishes.
covers: the S − rS trick on numbers
the general a/(1−r) and why |r|<1 matters

video.title: Why 1/n gets as close to 0 as you like, but never arrives
video.angle: for any target gap ε, pick n past 1/ε; the tail is trapped, yet every term is still positive.
covers: 1/n as a table and on the line
why the limit is 0 though no term equals 0

video.title: Why the sum of the first n odd numbers is always a perfect square
video.angle: each odd number is the L-shaped layer (gnomon) that grows an n×n square into an (n+1)×(n+1) square.
covers: setup: odd numbers and partial sums

video.title: Why sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, and where the sine wave comes from
video.angle: a point on the unit circle has coordinates (cos θ, sin θ); Pythagoras on that point is the identity.
covers: the unit circle and the point (cos θ, sin θ)
sweeping θ and tracing sin θ into a wave
cos as the same wave shifted

video.title: Why the sine addition formula works
video.angle: rotating the plane by α then β is the same as rotating by α+β; comparing coordinates gives the formula.
covers: rotation of a point by an angle
rotate by α, then by β
why trig equations then repeat every 2π

video.title: Why a triangle's angles always add to 180°
video.angle: a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side turns the three angles into a straight angle.
covers: the parallel-line proof on an acute triangle
same proof on a right triangle
same proof on an obtuse triangle
the alternate-angles fact it rests on
extension: exterior angle = sum of the other two

video.title: Why a quadrilateral's midpoints always form a parallelogram (Varignon)
video.angle: each midpoint segment is a midline of a triangle, so it's parallel to a diagonal and half its length.
covers: the midpoint quadrilateral drawn for a convex case
two opposite sides both parallel to diagonal 1
the other two parallel to diagonal 2

video.title: Why an inscribed angle is half the central angle
video.angle: split into isosceles triangles with radii; the exterior-angle step doubles the inscribed angle.
covers: central vs inscribed angle on the same arc
Thales: angle in a semicircle is 90°

video.title: Why a circle's area is π r²
video.angle: slice the disk into thin wedges and re-lay them as a strip that becomes a rectangle π r by r.
covers: the strip's dimensions: half the circumference by r

video.title: Why every analytic-geometry formula is Pythagoras in disguise
video.angle: the distance formula is the hypotenuse of a right triangle; the circle equation is 'distance = r'.
covers: distance between two points as a right triangle
line through two points from equal slopes

video.title: Why a cone (and a pyramid) is exactly one third of its box
video.angle: three congruent pyramids tile a cube; scaling and slicing (Cavalieri) carry it to cones and prisms.
covers: a cube cut into 3 equal square pyramids
the same 1/3 for any prism → pyramid
sphere = 4/3 π r³ by Archimedes' cylinder-minus-cone

video.title: Why n! counts arrangements and why C(n,k) = C(n,n−k)
video.angle: fill slots one at a time (multiplication rule); choosing who's in is the same as choosing who's out.
covers: choosing a committee vs choosing the leftovers

video.title: Why switching doors wins 2/3 of the time (Monty Hall)
video.angle: your first pick is right 1/3 of the time; the host's forced reveal dumps the other 2/3 onto the last door.
covers: 'at least one' = 1 − P(none) as a companion idea

video.title: Why conditioning shrinks the sample space
video.angle: P(A | B) just re-normalises: throw away everything outside B, then measure A inside what's left.
covers: P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B) read off the table

video.title: Why the mean chases an outlier and the median barely moves
video.angle: the mean is a balance point, so distance matters; the median is a count, so only order matters.
covers: a small data set: mean vs median
drag one point far right — watch both
the mean as a see-saw balance
why variance squares the gaps (a signed-sum would cancel)

video.title: Why the derivative is the slope of a vanishing secant, and why (xⁿ)′ = n xⁿ⁻¹
video.angle: shrink the gap h to 0: the secant slope settles on the tangent slope; expand (x+h)ⁿ and the n xⁿ⁻¹ term survives.
covers: why f′ = 0 marks a peak or valley

video.title: Why the contrapositive says the same thing, and De Morgan's laws
video.angle: 'if P then Q' and 'if not Q then not P' rule out exactly the same row of the truth table.
covers: a truth table for P ⇒ Q
